title: Turning Number and the Geometry of Disorder-Induced Topology
abstract: The geometry of momentum-space Hamiltonian maps derived from the zero-frequency single-particle Green's function provides a route to a refined topological characterization of quantum systems beyond the noninteracting clean limit. The central idea is to complement standard topological invariants by invariants that characterize the geometry of the map itself. As a paradigmatic example, we study the one-dimensional chiral Su-Schrieffer-Heeger model with disorder, where the topological Hamiltonian defines a planar Bloch loop. In addition to its conventional winding number, this loop possesses an integer turning number that characterizes the winding of its tangent vector. We identify turning-number transitions that occur while the topological Hamiltonian remains finite and spectrally gapped, driven solely by a vanishing tangent vector of the Bloch loop, and obtain an extended phase diagram with additional topological structure beyond the winding-number classification. Asymptotic analysis predicts the emergence and disorder dependence of the corresponding transition regime, in agreement with the numerical results. Our findings establish the geometry of momentum-space Hamiltonian maps as an additional source of topological structure beyond conventional classifications.
summary: This work introduces the 'turning number' ($	au$) as a geometric topological invariant to refine the classification of quantum systems beyond standard winding numbers. By applying this to the disordered SSH model, the authors show that $	au$ detects additional phase transitions driven by the geometry of the momentum-space Hamiltonian map, providing a richer phase diagram than previously known.
main_problem: To refine the topological characterization of quantum systems beyond the noninteracting clean limit by characterizing the geometry of momentum-space Hamiltonian maps.
main_result:
The turning number ($	au$) provides an additional topological invariant beyond the conventional winding number ($
u$), revealing phase transitions driven by the vanishing of the tangent vector of the Bloch loop, even when the gap remains open.
method:
The authors analyze the geometry of the Bloch loop traced by the topological Hamiltonian $H_{	ext{top}}(k)$ derived from the zero-frequency Green's function, calculating both the winding number ($
u$) and the turning number ($	au$).
model_or_system: The study uses the one-dimensional chiral Su-Schrieffer-Heeger (SSH) model subjected to disorder. The topological properties are encoded in the momentum-space Hamiltonian map $H_{	ext{top}}(k) = -G^{-1}(k, i\omega = 0)$.
key_observables:
Winding number ($
u$), Turning number ($	au$), Spectral gap, and the geometry of the Bloch loop $d(k)$.
important_parameters: Disorder strength ($W$), hopping ratios ($t_2/t_1$), and the momentum $k$ within the Brillouin Zone (BZ).
main_assumptions:
The analysis relies on the topological Hamiltonian derived from the zero-frequency Green's function, and the turning number is defined as the winding number of the tangent vector, which requires $\partial_k d(k) 
eq 0$.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate $	au$ transitions as a function of disorder and hopping ratios, show band structures for the clean limit, and display the disorder-averaged Green's function revealing gap reopening.
paper_structure:
The paper introduces the concept of geometric invariants ($	au$) to complement standard topological invariants ($
u$). It applies this framework to the disordered SSH model, demonstrating that $	au$ captures transitions invisible to $
u$, especially in the strong disorder regime.
why_interesting: The concept of using geometric invariants of momentum-space maps to classify topological phases is highly relevant for understanding complex many-body systems, including those studied in AMO physics (e.g., synthetic gauge fields) or condensed matter systems with engineered disorder.
